problems.label: Cannabis use that is hard to control and causes problems

definitions.text: Uses cannabis more often or in larger amounts than planned, and has tried to cut down without success.
Has strong urges to use and feels irritable, restless or sleeps poorly when stopping.
Use has caused problems at work, school, home or with mood, or has happened in risky situations such as driving.

longTermGoals.text: The client reaches their own goal for cannabis use (stopping or cutting down) and feels more in control of their mood, sleep and daily life.

shortTermObjectives.text: By session 3, set a personal goal for cannabis use and list 3 reasons for change in own words.
For 4 weeks, log use, amount and situation each day, and identify the 3 most common triggers.
Use urge surfing or another coping skill for at least 3 urges a week and record the outcome.
If available, join a program that offers incentives for meeting use goals.
By session 8, complete a relapse prevention plan with high-risk situations and coping steps.

collaborativeNote: Write goals and objectives with the client in their own words. Timelines and targets are examples to adapt; the client decides what matters, and the clinician checks safety and fit. Every item in this plan records substance use: the export carries the 42 CFR Part 2 notice.
